# Chapter 5: Computer components

<!-- BEGIN HEADER (generated by tools/build.py) -->
> [Home](../../../../README.md) › [Part I — Computer Science Foundations](../../index.md) › [1. Computer Fundamentals](../index.md) › Chapter 5: Computer components

- **Status:** Drafted · 10 syllabus topics
<!-- END HEADER -->

The earlier chapters described a computer abstractly: numbers, text, logic. This chapter opens the box and names the parts. It explains what the **processors** (CPU and GPU) do and why there are two kinds, what each level of **memory and storage** is for and why a computer needs so many of them, and how the **motherboard, power supply, network interface and peripherals** connect everything into one working machine.

One idea ties the chapter together: **every component is a trade-off between speed, capacity, cost and power**, and good systems are built by arranging components so that the fast, small, expensive ones are used for what matters most. You will meet the same idea again in operating systems, databases and distributed systems.

Read the lessons in order.
